title: Drummers Lovett admired: his brother, Buddy Rich, Jo Jones
summary: Lovett copied no one but his brother and now likes Buddy Rich and Jo Jones.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: -- I would have thought so, but the question was a good one. Baby, what older musicians did you pattern your music after?

Well, I don't know of any; only my brother. You know my brother was a drummer and he was a great drummer and I used to watch him play all the time. See, that's where I learned -- that's the way I learned drums, from my brother.
Well you were fortunate you had your
brother but if no older drummers influenced you, what about younger drummers?
Well, younger drummers, I don't know. I just -- just from my own ideas about playing drums you know. You notice right now, I don't copy after anybody.
I try to be just a little bit -- just to have something a little bit different from the other drummers, you understand?
It might be rotten but it's different, I'll put it that way.

Right. I wasn't talking about copying but there are certain drummers that I'm sure influence us; maybe not the same ones and I'm sure there are guitarists that have influenced Crook and vocalists that had influenced him.
Well, I'll tell you now, Buddy Rich is my drummer. I like his playing, yeah, Buddy Rich.
Well -- of course -- but of course there was nobody that you really --
And Jo Jones, wait a minute, those two are my drummers now.
Well you and Jo are real pals.
Well, I know. He stays at your house every time he comes to Kansas City.
